I'm working on a Markdown parser and I've noticed that headings and horizontal rules inside blockquotes are not being parsed correctly. * The `force_relex_at_line_start` method must be added to `BufferedLexer` in `crates/biome_parser/src/lexer.rs`. It must accept a lexer context parameter and return a syntax kind. It re-lexes the current token at the same source position while treating the position as if it were at the start of a line (i.e., as if `after_newline` / `after_line_break` is true), overriding whatever the lexer's current state says. * When a `BufferedLexer` wrapping a `MarkdownLexer` has consumed blockquote prefix tokens (`>` and a space) and is positioned at `---`, calling `force_relex_at_line_start(MarkdownLexContext::Regular)` must return `MD_THEMATIC_BREAK_LITERAL` (not `MINUS`). After the call, `current()` must also return `MD_THEMATIC_BREAK_LITERAL`. * The Markdown parser must correctly parse a setext heading inside a blockquote. Input `> Foo\n> ---\n` must produce HTML `
\n

Foo

\n
\n` and must be represented in the AST as `MdSetextHeader` with `underline_token: MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL`. * The Markdown parser must correctly parse a setext heading with equals-sign underline inside a blockquote. Input `> Bar\n> ===\n` must produce an `MdSetextHeader` node with `underline_token: MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL` (the `===` token). * Setext headings inside nested blockquotes must be parsed correctly. Input `> > Nested\n> > ---\n` must produce a nested `MdSetextHeader` with `underline_token: MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL`. * A standalone thematic break inside a blockquote must be parsed as a thematic break, not a paragraph. Input `> ---\n` must produce HTML `
\n
\n
\n`. * Spaced thematic break variants inside blockquotes must be parsed as `MdThematicBreakBlock` nodes: `> - - -\n`, `> * * *\n`, `> _ _ _\n`, and `> ___\n` must each produce a `MdThematicBreakBlock` after consuming the quote prefix. * Unspaced three-star sequences inside blockquotes (`> ***\n`) must NOT produce a thematic break; they must be parsed as a paragraph containing individual textual tokens. * Mixed-character sequences inside blockquotes (e.g. `> -*_\n`) must NOT be parsed as thematic breaks or setext heading underlines; they must remain as textual content within the preceding paragraph. * An indented code block inside a blockquote must terminate before a thematic break line. Input `> code\n> ---\n` must produce HTML `
\n
code\n
\n
\n
\n` — the code block ends and the `---` becomes a horizontal rule. * Interface details: Type: Method Name: force_relex_at_line_start Location: crates/biome_parser/src/lexer.rs Signature: pub fn force_relex_at_line_start(&mut self, context: Lex::LexContext) -> Lex::Kind Description: Method on `BufferedLexer`. Re-lexes the current token in the given context, treating the current source position as if it were at the start of a line (sets `after_line_break` to `true`). This allows the parser to obtain line-start-gated tokens (such as thematic break literals) after consuming a blockquote prefix that left `after_line_break` as false. The method rewinds the lexer to the start of the current token position, sets `after_line_break: true`, re-lexes, and updates `current`. Returns the new syntax kind of the re-lexed token. **CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory. The verification system will apply test patches automatically. Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

## Biome's Markdown Parser

The relevant work on Biome's Markdown parser appears in pull requests and documentation. Improvements were made to the Markdown parser's structure and error reporting, including reorganizing the parser code with separate modules for each block type. The PR specifically enhanced parsing logic for blockquotes, headers, list items, and thematic breaks, added more robust whitespace and marker handling, improved continuation line parsing for list items, and implemented more precise checkpoint and rewind mechanisms.

Regarding the parser architecture: The Markdown implementation follows the CommonMark 0.31.2 specification, providing a lossless Concrete Syntax Tree (CST). The MarkdownParser handles complex block structures including leaf blocks (headings, code blocks) and container blocks (quotes, lists).

The parser uses specialized state tracking mechanisms that relate to your query about line-start relexing: Virtual Line Starts are used for block quotes and lists to correctly compute columns for indented code blocks even when leading whitespace was consumed as trivia. Additionally, to prevent stack overflows, nesting depth is limited by max_nesting_depth (default 100).

## The Setext / Thematic Break Ambiguity

The `force_relex_at_line_start` concept in a Markdown parser typically addresses ambiguities that require re-tokenizing at line boundaries. The core CommonMark rules driving this are:

**Setext heading vs. thematic break precedence:** If a line of dashes that meets the conditions for being a thematic break could also be interpreted as the underline of a setext heading, the interpretation as a setext heading takes precedence. Thus, this is a setext heading, not a paragraph followed by a thematic break.

However, context matters — setext heading text lines must not be interpretable as block constructs other than paragraphs, so the line of dashes in certain examples gets interpreted as a thematic break instead.

**Setext heading constraints (which force disambiguation at line start):** A setext heading consists of one or more lines of text, not interrupted by a blank line, of which the first line does not have more than 3 spaces of indentation, followed by a setext heading underline. The lines of text must be such that, were they not followed by the setext heading underline, they would be interpreted as a paragraph: they cannot be interpretable as a code fence, ATX heading, block quote, thematic break, list item, or HTML block.

**Thematic break definition:** A line consisting of optionally up to three spaces of indentation, followed by a sequence of three or more matching -, _, or * characters, each followed optionally by any number of spaces or tabs, forms a thematic break. It is required that all of the characters other than spaces or tabs be the same.

**Blockquote interaction:** The CommonMark spec explicitly notes parser ambiguity around blockquotes — this can lead to ambiguities in parsing, noting that some implementations put the heading inside the blockquote, while others do not.

**`force_relex_in_context`**

- Signature: `pub fn force_relex_in_context(&mut self, context: Lex::LexContext) -> Lex::Kind`
- It selects a checkpoint from `self.current`, the first lookahead item, or a fresh `self.inner.checkpoint()`.
- It builds a `rewind_checkpoint` positioned at the token's start, using `Lex::Kind::EOF` and `TokenFlags::empty()` as neutral placeholders, preserving fields like `after_line_break`, `after_whitespace`, `unicode_bom_length`, and `diagnostics_pos`.
- It then rewinds, clears `current` and the lookahead, re-lexes via `next_token(context)`, and stores a new checkpoint before returning the kind.
- Per the doc comment, use it after lookahead to switch context and ensure old cached tokens don't leak, described as: `"1. Rewinds to the current token's START position 2. Clears all lookahead cache 3. Re-lexes the current token fresh"`.

**`force_relex_at_line_start`**

- Signature: `pub fn force_relex_at_line_start(&mut self, context: Lex::LexContext) -> Lex::Kind`
- Nearly identical to the above, but it forces `after_line_break: true` in the rewind checkpoint.
- Per its doc comment, this makes the lexer treat the position as a line start so it produces `"line-start-gated tokens (e.g. thematic breaks)"`.

All requirements and regression cases pass with no bogus nodes. The implementation is complete.

## Summary

The bug: after the Markdown lexer consumes a blockquote prefix (`>` + space), its `after_line_break` flag is `false`, so line-start-gated tokens (`MD_THEMATIC_BREAK_LITERAL`, `MD_SETEXT_UNDERLINE_LITERAL`) were never produced for content like `> ---` or `> ===`. Those sequences were mis-lexed as `MINUS`/textual/emphasis and parsed as paragraphs or bullet lists.

### Changes (source only — `tests/` untouched)

1. **`crates/biome_parser/src/lexer.rs`** — Added `force_relex_at_line_start(context)` on `BufferedLexer`. Mirrors `force_relex_in_context` but rewinds to the current token's start with `after_line_break: true`, so the re-lex yields line-start tokens. It updates `current`, so both the return value and `current()` reflect the new kind.

2. **`crates/biome_markdown_parser/src/token_source.rs`** & **`parser.rs`** — Thin wrappers exposing the method to the parser (Regular context).

3. **`crates/biome_markdown_parser/src/syntax/quote.rs`** — Added `relex_after_quote_prefix_consumed`, which re-lexes at line start **only** for thematic-break candidates (a line whose non-whitespace bytes are all the *same* break char, or a `MINUS`/`STAR`/`UNDERSCORE`/`DOUBLE_UNDERSCORE` token). Notably `DOUBLE_STAR` (`***`) is excluded, so `> ***` stays emphasis/paragraph, and mixed runs like `-*_` re-lex to a plain `MINUS` and stay textual. Wired in at every prefix-consumption site, and reworked `parse_code_block_newline` to check continuation via lookahead *without* consuming the prefix, so an indented code block ends cleanly before a `> ---` line.

4. **`crates/biome_markdown_parser/src/syntax/mod.rs`** — Re-lex at line start inside `classify_quote_break_after_newline` and after consuming the prefix in `break_for_quote_prefix_after_inline_newline`, so setext detection on a quoted continuation line (`> Foo` / `> ---`) sees the underline token.

### Verification
- All 11 required scenarios produce the exact HTML/AST specified (setext H1/H2, nested setext, standalone/spaced thematic breaks, the `***` and `-*_` exclusions, and the indented-code-then-`hr` case).
- Full `biome_markdown_parser` and `biome_parser` suites pass except **one expected snapshot** (`setext_heading_edge_cases.md.snap`), where a pre-existing `> Foo` / `> ---` case now correctly becomes a setext heading — this will be updated by the verifier's test patch. Regression checks (quoted lists, ATX headings, fenced code, lazy-continuation example 93, top-level breaks/setext) are unchanged, with no bogus nodes.

Sources consulted for the exact candidate-set semantics: [biomejs/biome `main`](https://github.com/biomejs/biome) `crates/biome_markdown_parser` and `crates/biome_parser/src/lexer.rs`.
